title: IntReal: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Multimodal Interleaved Generation
summary: Humans routinely consume multimodal content, where textual and visual information is naturally interleaved. Although Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) can jointly generate text and images, multimodal interleaved generation remains largely underexplored. Progress in this area is hindered by two key limitations: (1) the lack of well-defined interleaved generation tasks and corresponding training data, and (2) the absence of fine-grained evaluation protocols that can reliably diagnose model performance across different capability dimensions. To this end, we present IntReal, comprising two complementary components: IntReal-100K, a real-world dataset of multimodal interleaved samples spanning four major categories, and the IntReal Evaluation Suite, which evaluates model performance across seven complementary dimensions using specialized expert models, enabling coarse-to-fine diagnosis. Extensive experiments validate our evaluation suite through low inter-metric redundancy (max pairwise absolute Spearman's $ρ\leq 0.42$ ), high agreement with human judgments (83.3% accuracy), and strong consistency across different expert evaluators (Spearman's $ρ> 0.9$ ), supporting the complementarity and reliability of our metrics. By benchmarking four families of UMMs, we show that IntReal Evaluation Suite reveals distinct strengths and weaknesses across models. Post-training experiments demonstrate the utility of IntReal-100K for improving interleaved generation and further show that training unimodal generation can also benefit interleaved generation. These findings suggest that interleaved generation can benefit from modality-specific optimization, rather than requiring joint text-image training at every stage.
tldr: IntReal introduces a large-scale real-world dataset and a multi-dimensional evaluation suite to address the current lack of systematic benchmarks and metrics for interleaved text-image generation.
tldr_zh: IntReal 引入了一个大规模真实世界数据集和多维评估套件，旨在解决当前交互式图文生成领域缺乏系统性基准和评估指标的问题。

title: WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One Agent From Narration to Long-Form Video
summary: Producing long-form videos from narration requires interdependent decisions that remain coherent across shots. Existing agentic editors often use multi-stage workflows driven by general models, leaving the quality-cost trade-off of compact, task-adapted policies unclear. We address this gap with WeVisCut, a long-form script-to-video system that connects tool execution with policy learning. Its agent harness maintains shared production state so that tool feedback informs subsequent decisions and repairs. Because finished videos do not expose these decisions, our four-stage data pipeline combines editing inversion with verified replay to turn recovered editing intent into executable supervision. Applied to 3,750 finished videos, this pipeline yields over 130K training examples. We use this supervision to train a single 9B policy that coordinates production and recovers from failures within the same harness. Moreover, we introduce a 100-task benchmark and five metrics assessing editing quality and delivery reliability. Under a shared tool environment, WeVisCut substantially outperforms its base model and achieves comparable performance to Claude Opus 5 while using nearly 33x fewer generated tokens per successful output minute. It also outperforms task-matched native editors on our proposed metrics.
tldr: WeVisCut is a compact 9B policy agent for long-form video editing that utilizes a novel data pipeline to translate finished videos into executable production steps, significantly improving efficiency over general-purpose LLM-based editors.
tldr_zh: WeVisCut 是一款用于长视频编辑的紧凑型 9B 参数策略智能体，它通过一套创新的数据流水线将成片视频转化为可执行的编辑指令，在大幅降低计算成本的同时，实现了优于通用大模型的编辑效率与质量。

title: MEV: A Multi-Event Video Dataset for Long-Take Generation
summary: Current datasets for text-to-video generation are largely limited to short clips depicting a single event or coarse-grained captions. As a result, they provide limited supervision for modeling long-take temporal dependencies, often leading to temporally inconsistent generations when describing multiple events. In this paper, we introduce MEV, a multi-event video dataset designed for long-take video generation. MEV provides high-quality real-world videos where subjects can perform a sequence of distinct, non-overlapping events, featuring precise temporal boundaries and fine-grained procedural annotations. This event-centric discretization reduces confounding factors and enables models to support temporally localized conditioning and build long-take videos from atomic event units. Furthermore, we introduce a comprehensive annotation pipeline that segments videos into temporally grounded events, and generates structured captions at both the global level and the event level. In addition, under an event-centric evaluation protocol, we conduct multi-event generation experiments by fine-tuning on MEV with temporally grounded event conditioning, leading to improved long-take event transitions and more coherent content. We believe this work provides a publicly available resource for multi-event fine-tuning and event-centric evaluation, together with practical insights into learning from temporally structured video-text data.
tldr: The paper introduces MEV, a new dataset for long-take video generation that uses event-centric annotation to improve temporal consistency and structured conditioning in video models.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了一个名为MEV的视频数据集，通过基于事件的细粒度标注，旨在提升长镜头视频生成中的时间一致性与结构化控制能力。

title: Hierarchical Diffusion for Camera-controlled Autoregressive Video Generation
summary: We address the task of long-video, camera-controlled generation from a single image. The dominant autoregressive paradigm suffers from two key limitations: (1) error accumulation over time, as distant frames are conditioned on previously generated outputs rather than ground truth, leading to drift; and (2) ambiguity in how to incorporate camera control. Standard solutions to both--such as self-forcing and conditioning on explicit 6-DOF poses--either incur significant computational overhead or produce drifting scene geometries over time. We propose a simple and lightweight framework that combines autoregressive generation (WanAR) with hierarchical long-context denoising (FixAR). To enforce scene geometry remains consistent with input cameras, we draw from feed-forward novel-view synthesis and reformulate video generation as a warping-and-inpainting problem. To mitigate drift, we introduce a hierarchical denoising strategy in which different stages condition on different temporal histories. Specifically, we first generate frames conditioned on the immediate past, and then refine them using a second denoiser conditioned on a temporally subsampled long-range history to enforce global consistency. This fine-to-coarse scheme enables each generated frame to effectively condition on the full temporal context without incurring a prohibitive cost. Experiments on RealEstate10k and DL3DV demonstrate that WanAR+FixAR outperforms prior methods for camera-controlled long-video generation, producing results that are both temporally stable and consistent with input camera trajectories.
tldr: The paper introduces a dual-stage framework, WanAR+FixAR, that mitigates drift and maintains camera consistency in long-form video generation by combining autoregressive frame generation with a hierarchical, long-context denoising refinement.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了一个名为 WanAR+FixAR 的双阶段框架，通过结合自回归视频生成与分层长上下文去噪，解决了长视频生成中的漂移问题，并实现了精准的摄像机运动控制。

title: Self-Consistency Geometry Injection for Multi-view Consistent Image Generation
summary: Recent diffusion models have achieved impressive progress in single image to multi-view generation by synthesizing consistent novel views efficiently. Existing methods usually explicitly or implicitly couple geometry inference and texture synthesis, making generation vulnerable to inaccurate geometry prediction. Although several geometry-guided methods have explored decoupling, they usually treat predicted geometry as a fixed condition and do not explicitly model whether the geometry is reliable. We therefore propose Reliability-Guided Multi-View Generation (RGMV), which comprises a parameter-free Self-Consistency Geometry Gate (SCG) and a Reliability-aware Geometry Injection (RGI) module. Specifically, a geometry proposal generator produces multiple geometry predictions for the same reference image and target viewpoints under different stochastic sampling configurations. SCG measures their spatial agreement to derive a reliability map, which RGI uses to modulate the injection strength of geometry-conditioned residuals in the RGB synthesis model. Moreover, RGMV can adapt to different geometry proposal generators. As a result, RGMV preserves stronger geometric guidance in stable regions while attenuating unreliable geometry cues before they propagate into multi-view RGB generation. Extensive experiments show that reliability-aware geometry injection improves the geometric quality of multi-view generation. Code: https://github.com/WISLab-GDUT/RGMV.
tldr: RGMV introduces a reliability-aware framework for multi-view image generation that uses self-consistency across stochastic geometry predictions to modulate geometric conditioning, effectively filtering out unreliable spatial cues.
tldr_zh: RGMV提出了一种多视角图像生成框架，通过评估不同几何预测的一致性生成可靠性图，从而动态调节几何条件的注入强度，提升了生成质量。

title: V-CAPE: Visual Consistency Assessment for Product Image Editing
summary: Recent advances in generative image editing enable complex transformations such as background replacement, object manipulation, and pose adjustment from natural language instructions. However, verifying that these transformations preserve visual consistency, defined as the preservation of an object's intrinsic visual attributes, including geometry, texture, color, and fine-grained details, remains a largely unsolved problem. This challenge is particularly pronounced at scale, where manual inspection is infeasible and automated quality assessment (AutoQA) could become essential. In this work, we introduce Visual Consistency Assessment for Product Image Editing (V-CAPE), a large-scale dataset for evaluating visual consistency in generative image editing. The dataset consists of 40K unique source-target product image pairs, each annotated with binary accept/reject labels and structured failure modes capturing fine-grained inconsistencies such as geometric distortions, pose errors, and identity mismatches. V-CAPE combines real-world edited images with a synthetic subset constructed from 3D assets, enabling both realistic evaluation and controlled analysis. Vision-language models (VLMs) across all evaluated size categories on AutoQA achieve accuracy below 65%, indicating that the dataset poses a substantial challenge regardless of model scale. Our results highlight fundamental limitations of current models in verifying visual consistency under transformation, positioning V-CAPE as a benchmark for advancing fine-grained image editing evaluation.
tldr: V-CAPE is a large-scale benchmark for evaluating visual consistency in generative product image editing, providing 40K annotated pairs to address the limitations of current VLMs in detecting fine-grained inconsistencies.
tldr_zh: V-CAPE 是一个用于评估生成式产品图像编辑视觉一致性的大规模基准数据集，包含 40K 对标注图像，旨在解决当前多模态模型在检测细粒度视觉不一致性方面的不足。

title: Structure-retained low-rank adapters for weather synthesis
summary: Real-world deployment of computer vision models, particularly in outdoor scenarios, is often limited by environmental interferences, such as adverse weather. Improving model robustness across weather conditions is thus critical for reliability. However, sourcing high-quality data relevant to isolated weather effects is a significant challenge. Most datasets include changes in dynamic elements across observations of the same scene: subjects such as pedestrians and vehicles change between shots, while camera viewpoints vary. These aspects make it difficult to decouple solely weather-induced distribution shifts from the scene. In this work, we address this with a novel weather synthesis framework that utilizes structure-retaining Low-Rank Adapters (LoRA). We analyze the attention blocks in Stable Diffusion XL (SDXL) and identify where relevant structural information is mostly processed during image-to-image translation. Through an architectural analysis of SDXL, we learn structural LoRA matrices for the corresponding blocks and then leverage them for weather synthesis, eliminating the need for external conditioning such as ControlNet. Experimental results demonstrate that our method improves upon existing synthesis approaches, achieving greater realism while preserving structure. This provides a robust pipeline for generating high-fidelity training and evaluation data for outdoor computer vision applications.
tldr: This paper proposes a structure-retaining LoRA-based framework for weather synthesis in Stable Diffusion XL, enabling high-fidelity image-to-image translation without the need for external conditioning like ControlNet.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种基于结构保留低秩适配器（LoRA）的极端天气合成框架，通过在SDXL中引入结构性LoRA矩阵，实现了无需ControlNet等外部调节的高保真天气图像合成。

title: ETA-Motion: Efficient Topology-Agnostic Motion Diffusion via Sparse Joint Learning
summary: Topology-agnostic motion generation aims to synthesize motions for diverse characters with arbitrary skeletons. Unlike conventional motion generation, which assumes a fixed skeletal template, this setting must handle diverse joint configurations and inconsistent joint semantics across characters. Existing methods address this challenge through dense full-joint modeling, which incurs substantial computational cost and hinders learning transferable motion patterns across diverse skeletal topologies. We present ETA-Motion, a topology-agnostic motion generation framework based on sparse joint learning. Instead of learning motion from all joints, our method uses a compact subset of joints to reduce redundancy and trains the motion generator on the resulting sparse skeleton. To facilitate correspondence across diverse topologies, we introduce semantic joint embeddings that combine textual and visual cues, together with topology-aware training objectives for preserving skeletal structure. Although ETA-Motion is trained only on sparse skeletal observations, it supports full-skeleton motion generation during inference. Experimental results demonstrate that ETA-Motion outperforms existing topology-agnostic baselines while significantly improving efficiency and generalization to unseen motions and unseen topologies.
tldr: ETA-Motion is a topology-agnostic motion generation framework that utilizes sparse joint learning and semantic embeddings to synthesize motions for diverse, unseen skeletal structures efficiently.
tldr_zh: ETA-Motion 是一种拓扑无关的动作生成框架，通过稀疏关节学习和语义嵌入技术，高效实现了对任意骨架结构和未知拓扑的动作生成。

title: 3DCodeEdit: Benchmarking Instruction-Guided 3D Program Editing
summary: Language models increasingly create 3D content through code, with practical workflows often relying on editing existing programs rather than regenerating them, for speed and precise control. Such edits require understanding what a program builds and foreseeing how a change reshapes it, yet prior benchmarks mostly evaluate generation or simple edits against a reference. In this paper, we introduce 3DCodeEdit, a benchmark of 2,592 instruction-guided editing tasks over 108 Blender programs that construct objects entirely in code. Its edits range from parameter to structural changes, style redesign, and scene composition, and are judged from renders against human-reviewed checklists. Across 17 models, the average success rate is only 37%, and even the strongest models complete fewer than 60% of structural and style edits. As models become more capable, their failures shift to geometric foresight, where the code runs but builds the wrong shape. We therefore study whether multi-turn feedback can compensate for this missing foresight. Feedback from a separate reviewer model that describes how the renders differ from the request helps most, more than maximum reasoning effort or an agent harness, and can let a 27B model surpass the single-shot rate of a 2.8T-parameter model.
tldr: 3DCodeEdit is a new benchmark for instruction-guided 3D program editing in Blender, revealing that current LLMs struggle with geometric foresight and that multi-turn feedback significantly outperforms single-shot generation.
tldr_zh: 3DCodeEdit 是一个用于 Blender 程序化 3D 内容编辑的基准测试，研究发现大模型在几何预判方面存在严重不足，且多轮反馈机制能显著提升编辑成功率。

title: StepControl: Long-Horizon Human Motion Generation from Foot-Contact Schedules
summary: Controllable human motion generation has largely focused on specifying what action should occur or where the body should move. We study a complementary question: can full-body motion be controlled by specifying only when each foot contacts the ground? We introduce StepControl, an autoregressive diffusion model conditioned on a future binary left/right foot-contact schedule, without requiring target root and body poses, or semantic prompts. StepControl represents contact as explicit temporal events and injects them through dedicated cross-attention with classifier-free guidance. We further introduce a stochastic mixture noise schedule and warmup strategy for stable long-horizon autoregressive generation. Experiments show that StepControl follows prescribed contact timing more accurately than adapting existing spatially guided motion generators to contact constraints. It maintains effective contact control over long continuous rollouts and responds to edited schedules such as cadence changes, stop-and-go pauses, limping gaits, and bilateral jumping. Our results show that minimal foot-contact schedules provide an effective and intuitive temporal interface for controllable motion generation.
tldr: StepControl is an autoregressive diffusion model that generates full-body human motion by conditioning on foot-contact timing schedules, offering an intuitive temporal interface for locomotion control.
tldr_zh: StepControl 是一种通过脚部接触时间表来生成全身人体动作的自回归扩散模型，为运动控制提供了一种直观的时间维度交互方式。
